import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_64/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_64/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_64/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_64/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_64/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source2 and Source0 on Cust_id to get Customer_Name for each order
df = pd.merge(source2, source0[['Customer_Name', 'Cust_id']], on='Cust_id', how='left')

# Step 2: Join with Source1 on Ship_id to get Ship_Date (and Ship_Mode, but not needed)
df = pd.merge(df, source1[['Ship_Date', 'Ship_id']], on='Ship_id', how='left')

# Step 3: Join with Source3 on Ord_id to get Order_Date and Order_Priority (not needed for target)
# This join is required by operation history, but we only keep Ship_Date from Source1
df = pd.merge(df, source3[['Ord_id']], on='Ord_id', how='left')

# Step 4: Join with Source4 on Prod_id (to satisfy operation history, though no new columns needed)
df = pd.merge(df, source4[['Prod_id']], on='Prod_id', how='left')

# Now, transform columns to match target schema and types

# Target schema: ['Ship_Date': string, 'Customer_Name': string, 'Ord_id': integer, 'Prod_id': integer, 'Ship_id': integer]

# Convert Ship_Date to string in format DD-MM-YYYY if not already
# Source1 Ship_Date is in format like '20-10-2010' (DD-MM-YYYY), so keep as is
df['Ship_Date'] = df['Ship_Date'].astype(str)

# Customer_Name is already string

# Ord_id: source has format like 'Ord_1082', convert to integer 1082
df['Ord_id'] = df['Ord_id'].astype(str).str.replace('Ord_', '', regex=False).astype(int)

# Prod_id: source has format like 'Prod_8', convert to integer 8
df['Prod_id'] = df['Prod_id'].astype(str).str.replace('Prod_', '', regex=False).astype(int)

# Ship_id: source has format like 'SHP_1495', convert to integer 1495
df['Ship_id'] = df['Ship_id'].astype(str).str.replace('SHP_', '', regex=False).astype(int)

# Select only the target columns in order
target_df = df[['Ship_Date', 'Customer_Name', 'Ord_id', 'Prod_id', 'Ship_id']]

# Save to the target path without index
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_64/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_64/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_64/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_64/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_64/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_64/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source5_64_2 with Source5_64_0 on Cust_id
df = pd.merge(source2, source0, on="Cust_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source5_64_1 on Ship_id
df = pd.merge(df, source1, on="Ship_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source5_64_3 on Ord_id
df = pd.merge(df, source3, on="Ord_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source5_64_4 on Prod_id
df = pd.merge(df, source4, on="Prod_id", how="inner")

# Select and rename columns to match target schema exactly
# Target schema: ['Ship_Date': string, 'Customer_Name': string, 'Ord_id': integer, 'Prod_id': integer, 'Ship_id': integer]

# Convert Ord_id, Prod_id, Ship_id to integer by extracting numeric part after underscore
df["Ord_id"] = df["Ord_id"].str.extract(r"(\d+)").astype(int)
df["Prod_id"] = df["Prod_id"].str.extract(r"(\d+)").astype(int)
df["Ship_id"] = df["Ship_id"].str.extract(r"(\d+)").astype(int)

# Ship_Date is string, keep as is
# Customer_Name is string, keep as is

# Group by all target columns to ensure uniqueness and remove duplicates if any
df = df.groupby(["Ship_Date", "Customer_Name", "Ord_id", "Prod_id", "Ship_id"], as_index=False).size()

# The groupby with size() adds a 'size' column, drop it to keep only grouped columns
df = df.drop(columns=["size"])

# Write to target file
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_64/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
